title: Spreading a specified normal unipotent subgroup with nontrivial geometric fibres
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $K/F$ an algebraically closed field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $J$ be a smooth affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $J_K=J\times_{\operatorname{Spec}F}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $N\hookrightarrow J_K$ is a nontrivial smooth connected closed normal subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] which is unipotent: it admits a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which every point over every algebraically closed extension has nilpotent difference from the identity matrix. Nontrivial means not isomorphic to the identity group scheme $1=\operatorname{Spec}K$ with its unique group law. There exist a finitely generated $F$-subalgebra $A\subseteq K$ and a smooth affine group scheme $\mathcal N$ of finite presentation over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with a closed normal inclusion $\mathcal N\hookrightarrow J_A=J\times_F\operatorname{Spec}A$, such that its base change to $K$ identifies with the given inclusion $N\hookrightarrow J_K$. Here normality over $A$ means that the image on points is a normal subgroup of $J_A(B)$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$. For every algebraically closed field $E$ and homomorphism $A\to E$, the closed normal subgroup $\mathcal N_E\subseteq J_E$ is nontrivial, smooth, connected and unipotent in the matrix sense just specified. No connectedness or reductivity assumption on $J$, and no perfectness assumption on $F$, is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Exercise 3.4.1(i)-(ii), printed p.104, applied to the specified normal unipotent subgroup (no reductivity hypothesis is needed for the spreading assertion); Milne Corollary 16.24, printed p.332, and Section 6.45, printed p.135, for additive series over an algebraically closed field and extension closure. No Stacks tag states this combined normal-unipotent model assertion. Conrad local PDF WANTED; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf.

proof.text: The field $K$ is perfect: an algebraic extension of an algebraically closed field is trivial. Apply the perfect-field additive-series theorem to $N$. It is affine of finite type, since a closed subscheme of the affine finite-type $J_K$ has a finitely generated quotient coordinate algebra. Obtain $N=N_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq N_m=1$, with smooth connected terms and specified quotient isomorphisms $N_j/N_{j+1}\simeq\mathbf G_{a,K}$. Here $m\geq1$, since $m=0$ would give $N=1$. The affine normal-quotient theorem supplies faithfully flat finitely presented quotient maps $q_j:N_j\to\mathbf G_{a,K}$ with the specified kernel $N_{j+1}$. All terms have finitely presented coordinate algebras: a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$), so apply finite-type implies finite-presentation. The same argument applies to $J$ over $F$.

source.place: Corollary 16.24, printed p.331; Theorem 5.28 and quotient discussion, pp.104--105; finite-presentation input: Stacks Algebra Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation

proof.text: Index by the set of finitely generated $F$-subalgebras $A\subseteq K$, ordered by inclusion. It is nonempty, directed (adjoin both finite generating sets), and has union $K$ (adjoin a given element). Thus $\operatorname{Spec}K=\varprojlim_A\operatorname{Spec}A$ by the affine-limit theorem. These bases are affine, hence qcqs, and every transition is affine. Descend the finite family $N_j$ to finite-presentation qcqs models at a common stage using family descent. Apply affineness descent to their structure maps, and pass to a common larger stage, to make all models affine. Keep $N_m=1_A$, $\mathbf G_{a,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$, and $J_A$ as their specified models. Products are the actual fibre products of these models. Finite presentation of their coordinate algebras follows from the tensor-product base-change and composition clauses.

source.place: Tags 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit; 01ZM(1), lemma-descend-finite-presentation; 01ZN, lemma-descend-affine-finite-presentation; affine tensor presentation

proof.text: Use the arrow and equality clauses of spreading out on the chosen affine models and their actual products. Descend multiplication, inverse and unit on every $N_j$, the inclusions $N_{j+1}\to N_j$ and $i:N_0\to J_A$, and $q_j:N_j\to\mathbf G_{a,A}$. Impose associativity, both unit and inverse identities and the homomorphism identities as equalities on products with at most three factors. Include the conjugation map $c:J_K\times_KN\to N$ and its equality $i(c(g,n))=g\,i(n)g^{-1}$. This map exists because the given normality on every algebra gives a natural map into $N$; representability identifies it with a morphism. Descend that map and equality as well. There are finitely many arrows and identities, so successive applications of the two clauses and a common refinement suffice. In particular all identities hold as scheme morphisms, not only on field-valued points; the model of $J$ retains its original group law.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(2),(3), lemma-descend-finite-presentation, applied to group operations, homomorphisms, and the specified conjugation factorization

proof.text: Preserve the kernel assertions, rather than only the equations $q_j i_{j+1}=0$. At the stage just chosen form the actual affine fibre product $T_j=N_j\times_{\mathbf G_a}1_A$. It is finitely presented over $A$: if $N_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$, its algebra is $B_j/(q_j^*t)$. The inclusion induces $a_j:N_{j+1}\to T_j$. Over $K$, $a_j$ is an isomorphism by the kernel assertion in step 1. Descend its specified inverse $b_j:(T_j)_K\to(N_{j+1})_K$ by the arrow clause of spreading out, and descend $a_jb_j=1$ and $b_ja_j=1$ by its equality clause. After finitely many refinements, $N_{j+1}$ is exactly the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q_j$ at the stage. This construction uses actual fibre products throughout, so the kernel identities persist under every base change.

source.place: Tag 01ZM(2),(3), lemma-descend-finite-presentation: inverse arrows and both inverse identities for the kernel comparison maps

proof.text: Apply eventual smoothness to each structure map $N_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, eventual closed immersion to all subgroup inclusions including $i:N_0\to J_A$, and eventual flatness and eventual surjectivity to each $q_j$. Their limit maps have these properties by step 1 and the given inclusion. Every map is of finite presentation: for affine models $C=A[x]/(f)$, $B=A[y]/(g)$, a map $C\to B$ sending $x_i$ to $p_i(y)$ presents $B$ as $C[y]/(g(y),x_i-p_i(y))$. Thus the required local finite type or local finite presentation hypotheses hold, and all sources, targets and bases are affine qcqs. Refine successively to retain all the finitely many properties; smoothness, closed immersion, flatness and surjectivity persist by their base-change lemmas. Call the resulting ring $A$ and put $\mathcal N=N_0$. For every $A$-algebra $B$, the conjugation identity of step 3 shows $g\,i(N_0(B))g^{-1}\subseteq i(N_0(B))$ for every $g\in J_A(B)$; applying it to $g^{-1}$ gives equality. Closed immersion gives injectivity on all these points. Hence $\mathcal N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $J_A$.

source.place: Tags 01ZP, 04AI, 07RR, labels lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation, lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation, lemma-descend-surjective; lemma-descend-smooth; permanence: Morphisms base-change lemmas

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $E$ and $A\to E$. Base change gives smooth affine finite-type groups $(N_j)_E$, closed inclusions, and flat surjective finitely presented homomorphisms $(q_j)_E:(N_j)_E\to\mathbf G_{a,E}$ with kernel $(N_{j+1})_E$. Use the cited base-change clauses for smoothness, closed immersion, flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation. Products, units and inverse equalities in steps 3--4 give the asserted kernel after this base change. For completeness these maps represent the fppf quotients: for any $E$-scheme $T\to\mathbf G_a$, the pullback of $(q_j)_E$ is itself a flat surjective finitely presented covering on which the section lifts. Two lifts $x,y$ have the same image precisely when $x^{-1}y$ belongs to the specified kernel, since $q_j$ is a homomorphism and the kernel square is cartesian. Representable presheaves are fppf sheaves: every fppf covering is fpqc by the cited covering theorem, and compatible maps glue uniquely by representable fpqc descent. Thus the sheaf of right cosets is the represented sheaf of $\mathbf G_a$. This checks the exactness hypotheses needed in the next step without assuming surjectivity on every algebra's points.

source.place: Conrad Exercise 3.4.1(ii), explicit base-change verification using Morphisms base-change lemmas; quotient verification from the covering and cartesian kernel

proof.text: Induct downwards on $j$, starting with $(N_m)_E=1_E$, which is connected and unipotent. The additive group is smooth by affine-space smoothness and connected by connectedness of the affine-line fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}E$. It is unipotent in the required matrix sense via the faithful closed representation $z\mapsto\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&z\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; its difference from the identity squares to zero over every extension field. If $(N_{j+1})_E$ is connected and unipotent, the exact sequence verified in step 6 and algebraic-group property permanence imply that $(N_j)_E$ is connected. The smooth unipotent-extension theorem then implies that $(N_j)_E$ is unipotent in precisely the matrix sense in the item. Its hypotheses hold: $E$ is algebraically closed, all three groups are smooth affine of finite type, the kernel is a closed normal subgroup, and the quotient is the represented fppf quotient of step 6. This proves connectedness and unipotence of $\mathcal N_E$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1(a), printed p.149; Section 6.45, printed p.135, extension closure; affine-line inputs are the existing scheme-geometric lemmas

proof.text: Finally $m\geq1$, so $(q_0)_E:\mathcal N_E\to\mathbf G_{a,E}$ is surjective. If $\mathcal N_E$ were the identity group, every group homomorphism from it to $\mathbf G_{a,E}$ would be its zero section, whose image misses the point $1\ne0$. This contradicts surjectivity. Thus every geometric fibre is nontrivial. The ring $A$ is a finitely generated $F$-subalgebra of $K$ by its choice of index, and the finite-stage comparison isomorphisms identify $\mathcal N_K\hookrightarrow J_K$ with the given inclusion, since that arrow and its relations were descended together. No argument used connectedness or reductivity of $J$, or perfectness of $F$.
